## 3 Project Scope & Limitations: {#3-project-scope-&-limitations:}

### 3.1 Business Rules: {#3.1-business-rules:}

| ID | Rule Definition | Type of Rule | Static or Dynamic | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-01 | Passwords must be at least 8 characters long and include one uppercase letter, one number and one special character. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-02 | Email address must be unique in the system and cannot be duplicated with existing accounts. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-03 | Username must be unique across all users in the system. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-04 | OTP verification is required via email before account creation can be completed. | Process | Static | System Design |
| BR-05 | Password reset requires email verification and valid OTP confirmation. | Process | Static | System Design |
| BR-06 | Login-Required Actions |  | Static | System Design |
| BR-07 | Banned-User lose all interactive privileges (Reviews, chat, group management, major actions) |  | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-08 | Account balance must be sufficient for checkout, otherwise redirect to top-up page. | Business Logic | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-09 | Users can only write reviews for games they own in their library. | Authorization | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-10 | Review content must comply with community standards or will be rejected. | Content Validation | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-11 | Review content and recommendation (Recommend/Not recommend) fields are mandatory. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-12 | Review content must not exceed 8000 words. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-13 | Refunds allowed within 7 days of purchase AND if playtime \< 2 hours | Business Logic | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-14 | All required fields must be completed in a Form of Request or Thread | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-15 | Publisher Serial ID must be exactly 12 numeric characters. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-16 | Only Publishers can create game addition requests. | Authorization | Static | System Design |
| BR-17 | Publishers can only manage games that have been approved and belong to them. | Authorization | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-18 | Game price field must contain only numeric values. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-19 | Game tags must be selected from predefined available options. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-20 | Memory requirements must be entered as a number followed by "GB" (e.g., 8GB). | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-21 | Game submission must include at least one image asset. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-22 | Game files must be submitted in .zip format only. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-23 | Game .zip file must contain launcher.exe file. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-24 | Listed state can only be changed if currently opposite | Business Logic | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-25 | Game updates must follow the same rules as new game submissions. | Process | Static | System Design |
| BR-26 | Friend Code search field accepts only numeric characters. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-27 | Users cannot have more than 285 friends. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-28 | Mutual block status prevents request | Authorization | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-29 | Users can create maximum 10 group chats. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-30 | Each group chat can have maximum 50 members including the owner. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-31 | Group chat creation requires group name and minimum 2 initial members including owner. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-32 | Chat messages cannot exceed 8000 words. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-33 | Admin accounts are unique and can only be added through direct database insertion. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-34 | Admin can only ban users who are not currently banned. | Authorization | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-35 | Admin can only unban users who are currently banned. | Authorization | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-36 | Admin can only list games that are currently unlisted. | Authorization | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-37 | Admin can only unlist games that are currently listed. | Authorization | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-38 | New family creation requires subscription to a subscription plan. | Business Logic | Static | System Design |
| BR-39 | Family can have maximum 5 members including the owner. | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-40 | Total invitations is equal or less than total remain slots in Family members | Constraint | Static | System Design |
| BR-41 | Only family owner can share games with family members. | Authorization | Static | System Design |
| BR-42 | Game sharing availability depends on the current subscription plan (4 plans total). | Business Logic | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-43 | Only family owner can extend plan by subscribing to new plan when expired or upgrading current plan. | Authorization | Static | System Design |
| BR-44 | Only family owner can make changes in family. | Authorization | Static | System Design |
| BR-45 | Users can only join family through invitation. | Authorization | Static | System Design |
| BR-46 | Cannot purchase lower tier subscription plan if current plan is still active. | Business Logic | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-47 | All shared games become unplayable when family subscription expires. | Business Logic | Dynamic | System Design |
| BR-48 | Email address must follow the format:  \<\>@domain | Business Logic | Static | System Design |

##### *Table \- Business Rules*

# II. Overview {#ii.-overview}

## 1\. System Context  {#1.-system-context}

The Centurion Store is a web-based platform designed to facilitate the browsing, purchasing, reviewing, and publishing of digital games. It replaces manual processes by providing an online interface for users to manage their game libraries, publishers to submit games, and admins to oversee operations. The context diagram below illustrates the external entities and system interfaces for release 1.0.  
![Context Diagram][image2]  
Figure 1.1 Context diagram

| 2 | User | Registered users who can buy games, manage their library, etc… |
| 3 | Publisher | Entity that submits games and manages content. |
| 4 | Admin | System administrator who manages users and  games |

**Table 1-1: Screen Definition for Register Screen**

| \# | Field Name | Type | Mandatory | Max Length | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Email address | Text | Yes | 500 | Available email and no one have registered using this email |
| 2 | Age Confirmation | Tick box | Yes |  | Use for User to confirm that they meet age requirements |
| 3 | OTP Code | Number | Yes | 6 | An OTP code sent to user’s email |
| 4 | User Name | Text | Yes | Unlimited | Unique username |
| 5 | Password | Text | Yes | Unlimited | Display "\*" instead of clear character |
| 8 | Confirm password | Text | Yes | Unlimited | Check if confirm password matches with password |
| 7 | Country | Dropdown  | Yes |  | Select User Country |
| 8 | Continue | Button |  |  | Use data from username and password field to register to website |

### 

*![][image4]*

| UC ID and Name: | UC-01: Register a New Account |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: | LocPG | Date Created: | 24/07/2025 |
| Primary Actor: | Guest | Secondary Actors: | None |
| Trigger: | The user clicks the “Register” button on the application’s homepage. |  |  |
| Description: | This use case describes the process through which a guest creates a new account in the system. The user provides required details such as email, password, and name. The system verifies the input, sends a confirmation email, and creates a user profile upon successful verification. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: Guests have access to a valid email address. PRE-2: Guest is not already logged into an account PRE-3: Registration page is accessible |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: A new user account is created and stored in the system database. POST-2: Guest becomes a registered user. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | Guest navigates to the registration page from the homepage. The system displays the registration form. Guest fills in required field: email. Guests click the “Continue” button. System validates the input (e.g. checks whether the email is already used). The system sends a verification email containing an OTP and displays user detail form. Guest fills in required fields: OTP, username, password, confirm password, country. The system validates the input (e.g. OTP, username, password, confirm password, country). The system activates the account. The system shows a message that registration is successful: “Registration successful\!” The system redirects the user to the homepage. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | 3a. Guest chooses “Sign up with Google”. 4a. System redirects to the respective OAuth login. 5a. Guest logs into the Google account. 6a. System retrieves guest information from Google account. 7a. System creates an account and logs in the user. 8a. System redirects the user to the homepage. |  |  |
| Exceptions: | E1: Username already exists in the system. System will display an error message: “This username is already taken. Please choose another username.” E2: Email already exists in the system. System will display an error message: “Email is already in use. ” E3: Weak password. System will display an error message: “Password must be at least 8 characters long and include a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter, a number, and a special character.” E4: Username is shorter than three characters. System will display an error message: “Username must be at least 3 characters long.” E5: Username contains special characters. System will display an error message: “Username must not contain special characters.” E6: Username contains spaces. System will display an error message: “Username must not contain spaces.” E7: Password and confirm password do not match. System will display an error message: “Passwords do not match.” E8: Wrong OTP format. System will display an error message: “OTP must be a 6-digit number.” E9: Wrong OTP or expired OTP. System will display an error message: “Invalid or expired OTP.” E9: Wrong email format. System will display an error message: “Invalid email format.” |  |  |
| Priority: | High |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Estimated 100-500 times per day |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR1 BR2 BR3BR4 BR48 |  |  |
| Other Information: | None |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Users have stable internet connectivity during registration. |  |  |

| Description: | This use case describes the process through which a guest logs into the system using their account. Upon clicking the “Login” button, the system initiates a login flow. After successful authentication, the system retrieves basic user information. If the account exists, the system logs the user in.. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | PRE-1: The user has a valid Google account. PRE-2: The user is not currently logged in. PRE-3: The login page is accessible. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | POST-1: The user is authenticated and granted access to the system. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | User navigates to the login page. System displays a login form. User fills in required fields (e.g. username, password). System validates the input. System redirects the user to the homepage. |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | 3a. User clicks “Login with Google”. 4a. System redirects the guest to Google’s OAuth2 login page. 5a. User logs into their Google account and grant access. 6a. System retrieves user data from Google. 7a. System checks if a corresponding account exists: a. If yes, log in the user. b. If not, create a new user account with Google data and log in the user. 8a. System redirects the user to the homepage. |  |  |
| Exceptions: | E1: User enters wrong username or password. System displays an error message: “Invalid username or password.” |  |  |
| Priority: | High |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Estimated 300–600 times per day. |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR6 |  |  |
| Other Information: | None. |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Users have stable internet connectivity during Login. |  |  |

*![][image6]*

| UC ID and Name: | UC-07: Buy game |  |  |
| ----: | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Created By: | HuyTS | Date Created | 24/07/2025 |
| Primary Actor: | User | Secondary Actor |  |
| Trigger: | After user add game to cart, user can navigate to the cart page and can start purchasing all games added into cart |  |  |
| Description: | This use case describes the process of a logged-in user selecting a game, completing the payment process, and gaining ownership of the game in their account. |  |  |
| Preconditions: | ​**PRE-1**: The user must be successfully logged into their Centurion System account. **PRE-2**: ​The selected game must be available for purchase in the system. **PRE-3**: ​The user must have access to a valid payment method accepted by the system. |  |  |
| Postconditions: | **POST-1**: **On Success:** The user's account is updated to reflect ownership of the purchased game. The transaction is successfully recorded in the system's database. The user receives a confirmation of the purchase. |  |  |
| Normal Flow: | The user navigates to the store page of a specific game. The user clicks the "Add to Cart" and then "Purchase for Myself" button. The system displays an order summary, including the game title, price. The System check the Wallet Balance of User (sufficient) The System subtract the user’s account balance, and add to the Publisher’s account balance The System records the transaction details. The System displays a "Purchase Successful" message to the user and sends a confirmation receipt to their registered email. The System add purchased game (Library Entry) to the User’s Library |  |  |
| Alternative Flows: | **The user has enough Wallet Balance** 4a. The System check the Wallet Balance of User (insufficient) 5a. The user confirms the order and selects a payment method. 6a.The system securely redirects the user to the external Payment Gateway. 7a. The user enters their payment information and authorizes the 8a. transaction on the Payment Gateway's interface. 9a. The Payment Gateway processes the payment and sends a confirmation response (callback) to the System. 10a. The System verifies the successful payment response from the gateway. 11a. The System subtract the user’s account balance, and add to the Publisher’s account balance 12a. The System records the transaction details. 13a. The System displays a "Purchase Successful" message to the user and sends a confirmation receipt to their registered email. 14a. The System add purchased game (Library Entry) to the User’s Library |  |  |
| Exceptions: | **E1**: Payment Declined: At step 9a, if the Payment Gateway declines the transaction (e.g., insufficient bank balance), it informs the System. The System then displays a "Payment Failed" message to the user and allows them to try again with a different payment method. **E2**: User Cancels Payment: At step 7a, if the user cancels the transaction on the Payment Gateway's page, they are redirected back to the store. The order is cancelled. The System then displays a "Payment Failed" message to the user |  |  |
| Priority: | High |  |  |
| Frequency of Use: | Frequent |  |  |
| Business Rules: | BR-14, BR-15 |  |  |
| Other Information: | None |  |  |
| Assumptions: | Users have stable internet connectivity |  |  |

| 1 | Your family members | List | Yes | 5 | List of members in the family |
| 2 | Add family members | Button | No |  | Button used to add friends into family |
| 3 | Choose friends | List | No |  | Show list of user’s friends |
| 4 | Family members | List | Yes |  | Show all friends that user choose to send invitation |
| 5 | Send invitation | Button | No |  | Button used to send invitation to all friends that are selected in the Choose friends |
| 6 | Cancel | Button | No |  | Cancel current action |
| 7 | Sent Invites | List | Yes |  | A list containing invitations that haven’t been accepted |

# IV. System Design {#iv.-system-design}

## 1\. Database Design {#1.-database-design}

### 1.1 Database Schema {#1.1-database-schema}

\[Database Schema Images references via Images\]

### 1.2 Table Descriptions {#1.2-table-descriptions}

| No | Table | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| *01* | *User* | *Store User information including profile, wallet, and authentication details* *Primary Key: UserID*  *Unique Key: Email, Username*  *Foreign Key: RoleID* |
| *02* | *Roles* | *Store the Role in the website (Admin, User, Publisher, etc.)*  *PK: RoleID* |
| *03* | *Game* | *Store Game Information including system requirements and pricing*  *PK: GameID*  *FK: PublisherID* |
| *04* | *Publisher* | *Store Publisher information including payment and legal details*  *PK: PublisherID*  *FK: PublisherID (self-reference)* |
| *05* | *Tags* | *Store all the Tags for game categorization*  *PK: TagID*  *Unique Key: TagName* |
| *06* | *GameTags* | *Junction table between Tag and Game. Represent relationship Many \- Many*  *PK: TagID, GameID*  *FK: TagID*  *FK: GameID* |
| *07* | *Transaction* | *Store the information of a Transaction of an User*  *PK: TransactionID*  *FK: UserID* |
| *08* | *TransactionDetail* | *Act as an Item in Transaction, store the linking between Transaction and Game*  *PK: TransactionID & GameID* *FK: TransactionID*  *FK: GameID* |
| *09* | *Review* | *Store the information of a Review by User for a Game*  *PK: GameID, UserID*  *FK: GameID*  *FK: UserID* |
| *10* | *ReviewHelpful* | *Store helpful votes for reviews*  *PK: HelpfulUserID, ReviewGameID, ReviewUserID*  *FK: HelpfulUserID*  *FK: ReviewGameID, ReviewUserID* |
| *11* | *ReviewNotHelpful* | *Store not helpful votes for reviews*  *PK: NotHelpfulUserID, ReviewGameID, ReviewUserID*  *FK: NotHelpfulUserID*  *FK: ReviewGameID, ReviewUserID* |
| *12* | *Cart* | *Temporary stores the connection between an User and a Game, acting as a Cart* *PK: GameID & UserID*  *FK: GameID*  *FK: UserID* |
| *13* | *Library* | *Store the connection between User and their Purchased Game with playtime tracking*  *PK: GameID & UserID* *FK: GameID*  *FK: UserID* |
| *14* | *Media* | *Store the information of media assets for Games and News* *PK: MediaID*  *FK: GameID*  *FK: NewsID* |
| *15* | *Request* | *Store the information of various types of requests*  *PK: RequestID*  *FK: UserID* |
| *16* | *PublisherApplyRequest* | *Store the information of a request to become a Publisher* *PK, FK: RequestID* |
| *17* | *AddingGameRequest* | *Store the information of a new Game request for admin validation*  *PK, FK: RequestID* |
| *18* | *Feedback* | *Store the information of feedback/support requests*  *PK, FK: RequestID* |
| *19* | *AddingGameRequest\_mediaUrls* | *Junction table for media URLs in game requests*  *FK: RequestID* |
| *20* | *AddingGameRequest\_tags* | *Junction table for tags in game requests*  *FK: RequestID* |
| *21* | *Feedback\_mediaUrls* | *Junction table for media URLs in feedback*  *FK: RequestID* |
| *22* | *Friendships* | *Store friendship relationships between users*  *PK: User1ID, User2ID*  *FK: User1ID*  *FK: User2ID* |
| *23* | *FriendRequests* | *Store pending friend requests between users*  *PK: RequestID*  *Unique Key: SenderID, ReceiverID*  *FK: SenderID*  *FK: ReceiverID* |
| *24* | *Blocks* | *Store blocked user relationships*  *PK: BlockedID, BlockerID*  *FK: BlockedID*  *FK: BlockerID* |
| *25* | *Conversations* | *Store private conversations between two users*  *PK: ConversationID*  *Unique Key: UserID1, UserID2*  *FK: UserID1*  *FK: UserID2* |
| *26* | *Messages* | *Store messages in private conversations*  *PK: MessageID*  *FK: ConversationID*  *FK: SenderID* |
| *27* | *GroupChat* | *Store group chat information*  *PK: GroupID*  *FK: OwnerID* |
| *28* | *GroupChatMember* | *Store group chat membership with admin privileges*  *PK: GroupID, UserID*  *FK: GroupID*  *FK: UserID* |
| *29* | *GroupMessage* | *Store messages in group chats*  *PK: MessageID*  *FK: GroupID*  *FK: SenderID* |
| *30* | *DiscussionThread* | *Store discussion threads for games*  *PK: threadId*  *FK: GameID*  *FK: UserID* |
| *31* | *DiscussionComment* | *Store comments in discussion threads*  *PK: commentId*  *FK: ThreadID*  *FK: UserID* |
| *32* | *Notifications* | *Store user notifications*  *PK: NotificationID*  *FK: UserID* |
| *33* | *SessionLog* | *Store user login session information*  *PK: SessionID*  *FK: UserID* |
| *34* | *PasswordResetToken* | *Store password reset tokens with OTP*  *PK: TokenID*  *FK: UserID* |
| *35* | *EmailVerificationToken* | *Store email verification tokens with OTP*  *PK: id* |

## 2\. Code Packages {#2.-code-packages}

### 2.1 Package Diagram {#2.1-package-diagram}

#### *2.1.1: Back-end Packages Diagrams*

![][image83]

| No | Package | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *01* | *controller* | *store APIs and routes* |
| *02* | *dto* | *store classes that contains informations that shows to Clients* |
| *03* | *service* | *store classes that process Business logic* |
| *04* | *repository* | *store the interfaces to query data from Database* |
| *05* | *entity* | *store entities for mapping data from Database.* |

#### *2.1.2: Front-end Packages Diagrams*

![][image84]

| No | Package | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *01* | *UI Layer* | *Responsible for Render UI to Users* |
| *02* | *Application Layer* | *Manage global state* |
| *03* | *Data Layer* | *Handles data access, storage and retrieval operations* |
| *04* | *Utility Layer* | *Provide common utilities and helper function for the system* |
